Question: If the (convex) area bounded by the \(x\)-axis and the lines \(y=mx+4,\) \(x=1,\) and \(x=4\) is \(7,\) then \(m\) equals:
Solution:
Convexity tells us which shapes are allowed. If \(y=mx+4\) crossed the \(x\)-axis strictly between \(x=1\) and \(x=4\), the two portions between the line and the axis would be triangles meeting at one point. Their union would not be convex. Thus the line must stay on one side of the axis throughout the strip, possibly meeting it at an endpoint.

Its endpoint heights are \(m+4\) and \(4m+4\). Both are nonnegative exactly when \(m\ge-1\), and both are nonpositive exactly when \(m\le-4\). The vertical boundaries are \(4-1=3\) units apart. We can therefore use the trapezoid area formula, which also gives the correct area for a rectangle or a triangular endpoint case.

For \(m\ge-1\), the area is
\[
7=\frac32\bigl((m+4)+(4m+4)\bigr)
=12+\frac{15m}{2}.
\]
Solving gives \(m=-2/3\). This satisfies \(m\ge-1\); its two heights are \(10/3\) and \(4/3\), so the resulting region is indeed convex and has area 7.

For \(m\le-4\), the vertical lengths are the negatives of the endpoint heights. The area is
\[
\frac32\bigl(-(m+4)-(4m+4)\bigr)
=-12-\frac{15m}{2}\ge18.
\]
It cannot equal 7. These cases exhaust the convex possibilities, so \(m=-\frac23\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
